title: Garage Build Tracker — One Record Per Vehicle, Updates From the Shop Floor

sections.label: 1 · ONE RECORD PER VEHICLE
sections.note: Every vehicle gets a job number the moment it is booked, and the task list for that job type is created with it. Nobody has to remember what a full rebuild involves, because the checklist arrives with the car. This is what makes the rest of the system possible: one place the vehicle actually lives.

sections.label: 2 · UPDATES FROM THE SHOP FLOOR
sections.note: Your techs already take photos. They send one with a voice note or a line of text from their phone, and it becomes a written progress update on the right vehicle. Nobody sits down at a computer to update a system, which is the reason shop tracking usually dies in month two.

sections.label: 3 · THE CUSTOMER STAYS WARM
sections.note: Not every update is worth sending. Milestones and anything that changes the timeline go out with the photo attached, small stuff just logs to the record. Customers on long builds call because they are in the dark, and this is the cheapest way to stop that.

sections.label: 4 · NOTHING SITS STILL WITHOUT SOMEONE KNOWING
sections.note: Every morning it checks which vehicles have not moved, splits them by why, and puts one board in front of you. Waiting on parts is a different problem from waiting on customer approval, and both are different from simply forgotten.
